digest.component_or_area: LLM model classes and verifier resolution
propositions: Three separate verifier code paths (review_kernel/verify.py, completion.py, code-review.yaml) each independently select a verifier model using equality tests against DEFAULT_MODEL, causing non-default models to break the downgrade and silently run on the frontier model instead of the standard class.

resolve_model must call resolve_model_string to map reserved class names (trivial/standard/frontier) through load_class_slots() while returning unrecognized model strings unchanged, enabling YAML steps to declare `model: standard` and resolve to the configured class instead of a literal string.

code-review.yaml's verify step declares no `model:` key and thus defaults to cfg.model (frontier), losing both the standard class downgrade and the intended `temperature: 0` determinism for Pass-2; adding `model: standard` makes the class resolution and temperature setting real.

With provider-qualified model ids (e.g. anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 or bedrock:...), the equality rule `model == DEFAULT_MODEL` silently fails and the verifier stays on the frontier model even when a non-default provider is configured, duplicating the defect across multiple backends.

All three verifier paths must resolve the standard class regardless of cfg.model value, enforced by separate call sites consuming resolve_model_string rather than by a single interception point (which is blocked by circular import dependencies).
Literal model ids passed to resolve_model_string and appearing in workflow YAML must return unchanged to preserve backward compatibility with existing deployments.
